newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen moderately up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen moderately up on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares fell in higher trade and analysts expected a rebound on Monday in reaction to a three-session slide, with possible falls on the world exchanges leading to further falls in Warsaw later in the week.

The main market's WIG index fell 117.6 points, or 0.7 percent, to 15,969.9, and turnover rose 19.3 percent to 160.4 million zlotys ($53.3 million) on all three markets as 43 issues fell, 34 rose and 16 were flat.
Analysts said the direction of the bourse was likely to depend on the U.S. Federal Reserve's meeting, which might decide on a rate rise in the United States.

"It seems to me a possible rebound on Monday won't be sharp as there is still no demand for large-caps...a lot will depend on the situation on world stocks exchanges," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska SA.

Some analysts said some stock prices were likely to become attractive during the next sessions as the market has already fallen 12.9 percent since recording a three-year February 18 high of 18,339.4, which might stir some long-term buying.
Analysts said 15,500 privided a strong support for the index.
Stocks were mixed in 15.8-million-zloty ($5 million) Warsaw bourse continuous trade with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,607.9 points, 1.1 percent higher than at the regular session.
